clue.text: Surrender, rest one's limbs

definitions.meaning: to give up fighting and yield to the enemy
taken literally, to put down your arms and let them lie at rest

explanation.surface: A tired soldier gives up and lets their arms and legs relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop fighting and yield, while the literal phrase pictures someone setting their arms down to rest.

clue.text: Alan's replacing silver put into the pasta!

indicators.note: put into means one piece is placed inside the other
replacing means placing the letters of the name again, in a fresh order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S, taken as letters
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone called Alan has had silver dropped into the pasta dish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' reshuffles the name's letters to LASNA, and 'put into' places the metal symbol inside that after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is a type of flat, sheet-shaped Italian noodle dish.

clue.text: Risky to trouble old rose fancier

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener devoted to old roses finds it risky to make a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges RISKY and TO together. The definition is cryptic: supporters of the House of York in the Wars of the Roses took the white rose as their emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of York in the fifteenth-century civil wars favoured the white rose badge.

clue.text: Seat of government? No…

parts.note: a seat in parliament that is not on the governing side but faces it, where the party out of power sits

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is where the government sits, and is told no.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK Commons, the party out of power sits on benches facing the ministers, so this is the seat of the non-governing side.

clue.text: … the way a horse is saying no soundly?…

indicators.note: soundly signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: to say nay is to say no, so saying no is naying

explanation.surface: A horse seems to be refusing something with its noises.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to the clues around it. Saying 'nay' (no) sounds like the horse's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighing is the high whinnying call a horse makes, so it describes how a horse vocalises.

clue.text: … worry about horse entering river

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
GG is a child's word for a horse (gee-gee)

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a horse wading into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the container. Gee-gee is British nursery talk for a horse, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To niggle is to nag at or trouble someone in a small persistent way.

clue.text: Be unyielding, remain on mid-west land

parts.note: to remain is to stand, as in stand still
taken as written

indicators.note: mid asks for the middle letters of the following word only

parts.note: ground is land or earth

explanation.surface: A stubborn settler refuses to leave a patch of land in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-west' looks like the US region, but 'mid' takes the middle of WEST, giving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to refuse to retreat or give way in an argument or fight.

clue.text: Give a new designation tersely perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word is only one possible arrangement, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone renames a thing in a brief, clipped way.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is a title or name, so to give a new title is to style it again.

clue.text: Play school is an outrage

definitions.meaning: Sheridan's comedy The School for ..., read as the thing that play's school exists for
a shocking event that causes public indignation

explanation.surface: A children's playgroup is condemned as a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is cryptic: The School for Scandal is an eighteenth-century play by Sheridan.
explanation.definitionFit: A shameful affair causing public disgrace, and the subject of Sheridan's famous comic play title.

clue.text: Doing away with fighting

definitions.meaning: brawling, having a fight or tussle

explanation.surface: A ban on brawling is being brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapping means junking or abolishing, and a scrap is also a fist fight.

clue.text: Unable to explain why one was out of port

definitions.text: why one was out of port
definitions.meaning: the reason a sailor was away from harbour: on the ocean

explanation.surface: A sailor cannot account for having been away from harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means bewildered, and literally describes a ship on the ocean away from harbour.

clue.text: Profits in gas share-out

indicators.note: a share-out divides and redistributes, so these letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Gas companies distribute their earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains are earnings or proceeds made on top of costs.

clue.text: Had a break, idle day, oh fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means wild and fanciful, so these letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims how wonderful a lazy day off was.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a vacation is to have a break from work.

clue.text: Not in favour of having reservoir designed to destroy military vehicles

parts.note: anti means opposed to
a tank is a container or reservoir for liquid

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a reservoir scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a water planning row; TANK is both the reservoir and the armoured vehicle the weapon targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-tank weapons such as mines and rockets are built to knock out armoured vehicles.

clue.text: One in France thoroughly ill

parts.note: un is French for one
well means thoroughly, as in well shaken

explanation.surface: A French person is completely sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell is a gentle synonym for sick.

clue.text: Conservative outfit hits another model

parts.note: a rig or rig-out is an outfit of clothes

indicators.note: another signals a different version of the letters, so they are reordered

parts.note: T is the Model T Ford, a famous car model

explanation.surface: A clothing outfit becomes a hit for yet another fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges HITS with T into HTIST. Model T was Ford's famous early car.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-winger holds traditional political views, as a Tory does.

clue.text: Bird nuts

definitions.meaning: a grey migratory songbird known for laying eggs in others' nests

explanation.surface: Someone calls a bird crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous nest-parasite bird, and also slang for crazy.

clue.text: Liqueur that's fashionable in Accra perhaps with duck

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the other piece
perhaps hints at one of several ways to arrange the city's letters

parts.note: U means upper-class, so fashionable or acceptable
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A drink that is trendy in Ghana's capital is served with duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ACCRA to CRACA, and 'in' puts U inside it after the first C. Accra is the capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean orange-flavoured spirit named after an island in the Antilles.

clue.text: Arrest officer shortly on the river

parts.note: Capt is the short form of captain, an officer
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A captain is briefly detained on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize and take someone into custody.

clue.text: Physicist had one German beer-mug

parts.note: ein is German for one
a stein is a large earthenware beer mug

explanation.surface: A scientist drank from a German beer tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the famous scientist behind relativity.

clue.text: Sees naturally occurring mineral as a blot on the landscape

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at or sees
ore is rock containing a valuable metal or mineral

explanation.surface: Someone spots a mine whose spoil heaps spoil the view.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or sight that spoils its surroundings.

clue.text: From the north-east, yours truly and little sister getting retribution

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
yours truly is the speaker, me
sis is the short form of sister

explanation.surface: A person and their kid sister from the northeast face punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Greek goddess of vengeance, it means downfall or just punishment.

clue.text: Insect found amongst the micrococci, cad announced

indicators.note: found amongst means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An insect turns up among bacteria while a rogue makes an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found amongst' points into MICROCOCCI CAD ANNOUNCED, where the run spans all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud chirping bug of warm climates, known for its long underground life cycle.

clue.text: About to announce reissue

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to publish is to make known or announce publicly

explanation.surface: Someone is about to make an announcement about a new edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To print and issue a book again.

clue.text: The man in strange surroundings is cold

indicators.note: surroundings means the other piece is wrapped around this one

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man feels chilly in unfamiliar surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' signals the container. Rum meaning odd is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery mucus, the discharge associated with a head cold.

clue.text: Milk can make butter…

definitions.meaning: a large metal container for carrying milk
to agitate cream until it turns solid

explanation.surface: Milk can be turned into butter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'can' as a verb; it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a large dairy container and the act of beating cream into a solid.

clue.text: … a little tart

parts.note: slightly sour or sharp in taste, rather than a small pastry

explanation.surface: Following on from making butter, a small pastry is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the butter-making clue, so 'tart' looks like a pastry; it is the taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat sour or acidic in flavour.

clue.text: Nothing to write, listen to Edward Head with cordiality

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pen is to write
to hear is to listen to
Ted is a pet form of Edward
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone is told to write nothing and pay attention to Edward the headmaster warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a school head; it is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth, friendliness and generosity of spirit.
